answer: On a basalt island, a cooperative buys trellis inspections from agents. Before assignments are revealed, inspectors reserve collateral for a fixed number of jobs. A random beacon then assigns sites and hidden control images; independent reviewers verify findings against dated photographs. Each site-period earns only one reward, even across aliases, and forged evidence provably linked to an inspector burns its bond. A hundred identities need a hundred funded slots and distinct inspections; copying names or reports cannot increase paid capacity.
